observations.finding: Composite of 2 treated fields vs DMSO (identical display): cell density appears similar to slightly lower in treated, confluence retained. No obvious cytotoxic clearing.
Cell size visibly increased in treated vs DMSO. Treated cells have larger cytoplasmic spread (green tubulin + red actin area), consistent with cell_area z=7.8 and cell_major_axis z=8.8 increase.

DNA (DAPI, blue in composite): marked nuclear enlargement in treated vs small uniform round nuclei in DMSO. Many nuclei ~1.5-2x larger, frequent bilobed / double nuclei within one cytoplasm and irregular contours. Fraction of large nuclei strongly increased.
Nuclear shape: treated nuclei more irregular/lobed and less round vs round/oval DMSO nuclei. Reduced circularity and outline regularity.

DNA (DAPI) integrated brightness/area: treated nuclei show larger and more intense blue signal, consistent with increased total DNA content per nucleus/cell. Nuc_area z=27.7, nuc_major_axis z=11.9, nuc_dna_integrated z=18.1.

Beta-tubulin (green in composite): microtubule network appears intact in treated, similar intensity and interphase radial organization to DMSO. No obvious depolymerization, bundling or monopolar spindles at this view; no strong mitotic arrest visible.
F-actin (red in composite): cortical actin and cell edge ruffles similar intensity to DMSO. No obvious loss of stress fibers, no punctate aggregation or strong cortical increase; pattern unchanged.

notable_cells.why: field-wide large bilobed nuclei exemplify polyploidy

candidate_mechanisms.why: Large irregular nuclei + greatly increased frac_large_nucleus (z 106), nuc_area, reduced form-factor/solidity, increased DNA integrated and increased cell size without microtubule loss is classic failed-cytokinesis polyploidy produced by Aurora kinase inhibition.
Other listed MoAs would show distinct tubulin/actin changes: not observed; phenotype alone could also overlap DNA replication stress but Aurora best fits.

report.uncertainty: Composites only, no single-channel grayscale quantitation; tubulin/actin changes could be subtle. Two fields of same low concentration (0.03 uM) show consistent phenotype.

observations.finding: Nuclei (blue in composite; no separate grayscale provided, read at identical contrast) appear brighter and more intense than DMSO. Many nuclei appear enlarged/bright. Cell number per field markedly lower than DMSO confluent monolayer - treated fields show sparse small clusters vs DMSO spread monolayer.

Integrated DNA per nucleus and mean DNA intensity strongly increased. Measured nuc_dna_integrated z=41.9 value 851 vs DMSO median 315 and nuc_dna_mean z=26.8 value 0.924 vs 0.414. Visible as bright saturated blue nuclei in composites.

Nuclear shape slightly more irregular/lobed, less circular. Measured nuc_form_factor z=-16.4 value 0.891 vs 0.916. Visible as non-round blue contours in clusters.

Cell shape markedly rounder, more solid, shorter major axis, less eccentric/elongated. Measured cell_roundness z=37.6 0.828 vs 0.525, cell_solidity z=37.4 0.954 vs 0.83, cell_major_axis z=-14.2 44.1 vs 89.9 px, cell_eccentricity z=-12.1 0.634 vs 0.774. Instead appears as numerous small bright punctate dots scattered across entire field, including cell-free background. Indicates loss/fragmentation of microtubule cytoskeleton. No tubulin feature in measured top_deviations - this observation is NOT covered by measurements.

F-actin (red in composite; read from colour only) appears largely absent/dim in treated fields vs strong red cortical staining, stress fibers and lamellipodia in DMSO. Treated fields show black background with negligible red. No actin feature in measured top_deviations - this observation is NOT covered by measurements.

No separate grayscale channels provided; assessment of blue/green/red from composite only. Cell loss/sparseness (cells_measured 188 for well) not listed as top_deviation vs DMSO - flagged as NOT covered by measured top_deviations (no cell_count z-score provided).

Specimen s_f499767749 (AZ841) unblinding confirms prediction: Aurora kinase inhibitors.

Evidence recap: Low doses (0.03-3 µM) showed extreme large-nucleus fraction (frac_large_nucleus z=58-106), enlarged irregular nuclei (nuc_area z 23-27, nuc_form_factor z -36 to -43, nuc_solidity strongly negative), increased DNA content (nuc_dna_integrated z ~18) with enlarged spread cells and intact microtubules (Microscopist e6). High dose (30 µM) shifted to rounded compact cells (cell_roundness z 37.6, solidity 37.4, major_axis -14) with further DNA accumulation (nuc_dna_integrated z 41.9). Atlas: 9/10 neighbors Aurora kinase inhibitors (AZ258, AZ-A), similarity 0.965 (e8), vs 1 microtubule destabilizer at 0.78.

Literature concordance: Aurora kinase function and inhibition linked to cytokinesis failure/polyploidy - e.g., Ma & Poon review of Aurora kinases and DNA damage response (PMID 32738522) and AURORA-A loss-associated multinucleation (PMID 30050055), consistent with BBBC021 annotation and observed bilobed/large nuclei phenotype. No ChEMBL curated MoA for AZ841, but image-based profile is canonical Aurora inhibition.

reflection.text:
Unblinded as AZ841 (CID 12001839, from BBBC021 structure, no ChEMBL curated mechanism per e15) -> truth Aurora kinase inhibitors. Verdict approve, correct call at p=0.94. What got it right:

1. Measurements: The quantitative phenotype was unequivocal and reproduced across log-spaced acquisitions. e5 dose 1 (0.03 uM): frac_large_nucleus z=+106.8, nuc_form_factor z=-43.2, nuc_solidity z=-30.1; e4 dose 3 (0.3 uM): frac_large_nucleus z=+76.8; e3 dose 5 (3 uM): frac_large_nucleus z=+59.0; e2 dose 7 (30 uM): nuc_dna_integrated z=+41.9. This pattern - huge, irregular, DNA-rich nuclei with negative form_factor/solidity - is the classic Aurora B failure-of-cytokinesis polyploid/bilobed phenotype, consistent with literature on Aurora inhibition and multinucleation PMID 30050055 and general Aurora inhibitor biology PMID 19369091 and PMID 22242557. We correctly weighted magnitude over monotonicity.

2. Comparison: e8 compare_to_reference_atlas was decisive: 9/10 nearest neighbors Aurora kinase inhibitors, 1/10 Microtubule destabilizer. With similarity 0.965 mean 0.912 per review, vs 0.78 for the single microtubule hit, this discriminated the main runner-up. e6 and e7 describe_phenotype both listed Aurora candidates (e6: candidates Aurora, unknown with density similar vs DMSO and 7 observations of intact microtubules; e7: Aurora + DNA damage/replication with density lower at high dose). Visual intact microtubule network contradicted microtubule destabilizers despite e8 containing 1/10 such hit.

3. Acquisition choice: list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.01-30 uM with 4-well budget. Sampling 0.03, 0.3, 3, 30 uM captured the biphasic dose-response that could have misled. e9 frac_large_nucleus rho=-1.00 (p=0) and e10 nuc_area rho=-1.00 show decreasing but still hugely positive z with increasing dose, while e12 cell_roundness rho=+1.00 shows increasing rounding and e2 cell_roundness z=+37.6 / cell_solidity z=+37.4 at 30 uM. Without the low-dose wells e5/e4 we would have seen only the high-dose rounded, lower-cell-count (188 vs 425 at 0.3 uM) secondary phenotype and risked calling mitotic arrest/DNA damage. Without high dose we would have missed the biphasic warning. e11 nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.80 p=0.2 was non-significant monotonic but absolute z 18-42 supported polyploidy at all doses; we did not over-interpret p-values.

What misled / what we missed:

Runner-ups DNA damage 0.01 and DNA replication 0.01 in e13 were correctly down-weighted, but they were plausible from e2 alone (high DNA content could be DNA damage/replication stress) and e7 microscopist included them. Discrimination relied on atlas and irregular nuclei morphology rather than direct DNA damage marker, which we did not have. We also had no direct target assay; e16 PubMed 'AZ841 Aurora' returned 4463 hits non-specific and e17 polyploidy search returned only 2 hits, so literature could not annotate AZ841 specifically - we relied entirely on phenotypic atlas plus morphology, appropriately leaving 0.06 uncertainty in e13/e14.

We did not acquire the lowest dose 0.01 uM or intermediate replicates to test potency or heterogeneity of bilobed vs multinucleate nuclei, and we did not measure phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 (Aurora B substrate) or ploidy by flow as proposed in next_experiment. Those would be required in a real lab to exclude composite phenotype limits noted in the review.

Calibration was appropriate: very large effect sizes (z +32 to +107) + 9/10 atlas + visual confirmation justified 0.94, not 1.0, given no biochemical validation.
